bordercontrol · Nov 21, 2026

I have been working on web applications for 15+ years and work in IT security. I am also a long-term user of 1984. I host my domains there and promote their service.

What most likely happened here is that they didn't have their software up to date. I highly doubt there was an undisclosed 0-click RCE involved in any of this. I have recently seen quite a few services I personally used that ran outdated versions of popular software and were vulnerable to some publicly disclosed RCE. I immediately notice these things, as I am auditing these types of services all the time. There is currently at least one major company in Switzerland that takes weeks to update their front end. They are vulnerable to RCEs all the time. This is nothing special currently.

Also, the talk of massive costs makes no sense. It's something they have not seen in Iceland, maybe, but it's normal, and the costs are extremely low, not millions. Probably just someone with a single Chinese AI subscription. Seeing complex attacks carried out extremely fast or with a huge number of requests doesn't indicate high costs by any means.

I have personally also recently developed such an exploit in this challenge (and won): [https://brotli2bitcoin.com/](https://brotli2bitcoin.com/). It did take expertise to set up the agents (basically letting them do the exact same thing I would have done, using the same approach), but ultimately, it took 37 minutes and, I think, would have cost me around 11 USD in tokens if billed at the API rate. I could have sped it up to maybe 5–10 minutes if I had been very dedicated and split the work further between agents. As I have a subscription, the effective cost was closer to a few cents.

I can't say if they are willingly or unwillingly trying to deflect responsibility away from themselves, but until they prove that they were hit by an undisclosed RCE, this is just poor maintenance on their part. We need to start holding companies responsible for not updating their software on time. They shouldn't be allowed to always play victim. The journalist should ask about their CI and when they last patched their software. That's what would let us judge them.
